summary: All three review reports' findings were re-checked against the fix report and the current branch head (d8ff391a8). Every blocker-severity test regression is genuinely fixed and re-verified by this recheck: the 80-cell CI regression (L05-SPEC-01/ADV-L05-01) is 0 red across every file the reviews named plus a broader 50-file/354-test sweep of everything that imports the touched fixture helpers, and operation-census/rig-isolation, typecheck, lint (CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true), check-frozen-workflows, check-parts-parity, check-message-keys, the runtime belt-isolation suite and the adjustments-retired-walk e2e (2/2, real built bundle) all pass on this recheck. L05-SPEC-04 (false runtime comments) and ADV-L05-05 (dead-end due banner) are fixed and independently re-verified in code and by re-run. ADV-L05-09 (stale page comments) is fixed. F1 (standards, commit-order disclosure) is satisfied by the fix report's own text. The fix round's own self-audit commit (d8ff391a8) found and correctly fixed two real defects in its first answer to ADV-L05-02 (a per-wake-kind blind spot in the containment tripwire, and a false claim about how the path is held shut) -- both re-verified here against the live catalog and the migration header/README/CONTEXT.md text, which now agree with each other and with what is actually measurable on clara_l05. No newly broken cell, migration or claim was found anywhere in the diff between the review head and the recheck head. What remains open is not a regression but three pre-existing majors/blockers the fix round could not close within lane scope and says so: the agent-lane prepayment path can still mint a 0045 template that no door can sign, run, sweep or warn about (still reachable, now contained by a tripwire test and documented in three places, but not closed -- closing it is a product-capability decision the lane is not authorized to make per WORK-ORDER rule 5); the sibling-plan advisory's self-exclusion-by-basis-identity still hides a total-overlap case this rig's own seed produces; and the advisory still has an unclosed concurrency window. All three are honestly disclosed, backed by a proposed fix and a named follow-up, and deliberately left for an owner/orchestrator ruling rather than coded around -- but per the recheck instruction to accept only when nothing above minor remains, they keep this from a clean accept.

findings.title: The agent-lane prepayment path can still mint an unreachable 0045 adjustment template; contained and disclosed, not closed
findings.evidence: Re-verified on clara_l05: clara._propose_adjustment_template_core is granted only to clara_fn_owner; clara.wake_establish_prepayment_schedule is granted to clara_wake_interactive and is the ONLY row in clara.wake_fn_allowlist for that function (array_agg = {close_prep}); clara.wake_engine_sources.close_prep.enabled = false. packages/db/tests/plan-overlap-template-arm-retired.test.mjs's p929.containment cell (re-run here, 4/4 pass in that file) asserts all three facts positively and proves each with a rolled-back mutant (widening the allowlist to a second kind, flipping the enabled flag). The commit d8ff391a8 in this same fix round found and fixed two real defects in the first answer to this finding: the tripwire originally counted the allowlist pair rather than reading it per wake kind (blind to a second-kind registration), and 0283's header / README.md / the cell's own message originally claimed 'no close_prep wake task is minted' when clara_l05 in fact carries 771 close_prep credentials minted by the batteries themselves and clara.mint_wake_credential_for_task never reads the flag -- the real gate is the runtime's claim step (packages/runtime/lib/wake-engine.mjs:392-397 and :801-804). Both corrections are now consistent across 0283's header, packages/db/README.md and the test file's own comments, and I independently confirmed each of the three underlying facts against the live catalog rather than trusting the prose. What is NOT true, and the fix report does not claim it is: the path is closed. A row can still be proposed today by any caller of the wake door with close_prep unparked, and #927/#928/#929 leave it un-signable, un-runnable, un-sweepable and un-advised.
findings.why_it_stays_open: Closing it means revoking a grant or refusing inside a core that a still-published successor door (clara.create_prepayment_schedule, 0223) exists for -- a product-capability retirement the #788 owner ruling never named, which WORK-ORDER rule 5 ("no migration in a wave-1 lane... a ticket that needs one, stop... and go on") and rule 5's scope-discipline reading put outside this fix round's authority. The fix round's own required_fix alternative (spec review's ADV-L05-02) explicitly allows leaving it open IF the reports state the residual in one sentence, which they now do in three places (migration header, README, CONTEXT.md _Avoid_ line) plus a named follow-up for the orchestrator.
findings.required_fix: Not a code fix owed to this lane. An owner/orchestrator ruling is owed: either retire or reroute clara.wake_establish_prepayment_schedule onto clara.create_prepayment_schedule (0223) in a ticket that owns that migration, or explicitly rule the residual acceptable and close the follow-up. Until that ruling lands, this stays a documented, tripwired, open item -- not a defect newly introduced by this fix round, and not silently dropped, but still open.

findings.title: The plan-overlap advisory's concurrency window (two concurrent creations both see NULL) is unchanged; correctly stated where the claim lives, not fixed
findings.evidence: 0283's header (re-read at HEAD) states the window explicitly and names the closing shape (the client-level pg_advisory_xact_lock pattern clara.retire_adjustment_template already uses). No code change addresses it. The three plan-creating doors (create_accounting_plan, revise_accounting_plan, _accrual_plan_core) are re-confirmed byte-unchanged in this recheck's own test run (plan-overlap-template-arm-retired.test.mjs's p929.tail cell re-derives all three shas and they match the pinned values). The fix report is honest that this is unfixed, not that it is fixed.
findings.why_it_stays_open: The honest fix recuts three function bodies that 0280/0281/0282/0283 all pin byte-unchanged, two of which are below the redo frontier and cannot be re-applied without a new migration -- explicitly a ticket per WORK-ORDER's migration and scope-discipline rules, not a fix-round edit.
findings.required_fix: File the follow-up (widen the three doors to take an advisory lock keyed on client_id, as 0283's header already specifies) as its own ticket; no action owed inside this lane's fix round.
